transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because for a long time now I just... I wake up already feeling really low. It's like there's this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic. I work as a medical assistant, actually, mostly taking vitals and rooming people. The commute to get there is pretty bad though, like, the bus system in this city is just getting worse every year. Yesterday I waited forty minutes in the rain because the transit app said it was two minutes away, and my shoes got completely soaked through. I had to wear these weird blue paper booties over my socks all shift just so I wouldn't squeak down the hallways... but, um, yeah, what was I saying? Right, that heavy gray feeling. It pretty much just follows me through the whole day, no matter what I'm doing.
How long have you been waking up with this heavy, gray feeling?

Well, let's see... it's been going on for about two years and two months. It all started right around the time the clinic staffing changed and they started rotating my schedule all over the place. Honestly, that whole staffing change was a mess. They brought in this new office manager, Brenda, and she decided everyone needed to be "cross-trained," which really just meant nobody knew what they were supposed to be doing on any given day. One day I'm up front dealing with insurance rejections—which, don't even get me started on prior authorizations, they take hours and half the time the fax machine jams—and the next day I'm back in the lab trying to figure out where someone moved the butterfly needles. And Brenda, she has this habit of leaving these passive-aggressive sticky notes everywhere instead of just talking to you. Like, I found a yellow Post-it on my keyboard that just said "Please remember protocol" with a smiley face. What protocol? But anyway, yeah, it's been a little over two years of waking up like this.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't even really remember what I used to do for fun... I guess I used to play video games a lot? But my controller has this horrible stick drift right now. It's the left analog stick, so every time I try to just stand still in a game, my character slowly walks into a wall. I tried fixing it by watching this YouTube tutorial, but the guy in the video had this tiny, specialized screwdriver set. I didn't have one, so I tried to use a butter knife from the kitchen. It totally stripped the screw and scratched up the plastic. 

And then my roommate got all annoyed because apparently it was *his* butter knife, even though we're supposed to be sharing the silverware. He's been super weird about the kitchen stuff lately anyway, like he started writing his initials on the bottom of the coffee mugs with a Sharpie. Who does that? It just washes off in the sink anyway when the water gets hot enough... but, um, sorry, what did you ask me?
Do you currently enjoy playing video games?

Um, no, not really. I don't enjoy them anymore. Even if the controller wasn't broken, I just... I sit down and stare at the screen and it just feels pointless. It's like, what's the point of leveling up a character when I can barely get myself out of bed, you know? 

Speaking of bed, my mattress is just awful. It's got this huge dip right in the middle, kind of like a crater. I bought it cheap off this guy on Craigslist, which was probably my first mistake. We had to strap it to the roof of my friend's sedan, and we didn't have real bungee cords, so we used these old extension cords we found in his trunk. I was so sure it was going to fly off on the highway and cause some massive pileup. But we made it back. Only now I wake up with this crick in my neck every single morning, and I swear it's making that heavy, gray feeling even worse. I tried putting a piece of plywood under the mattress to firm it up, but then it just felt like sleeping on a literal board... and the plywood smelled like weird chemicals, like glue or something. So yeah, I don't really play games anymore. I just kind of lay there in the dip.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure or enjoyment in?

No... I can't really think of anything. I mean, I thought maybe I could try reading again? Like, I used to read a lot of comic books. So I actually drove down to the shop on 4th street a couple weeks ago to see if that would spark something. But the parking down there is just impossible now. They installed all these new digital meters where you have to type in your license plate number, and I can never remember mine. It's just a random jumble of letters and numbers. My old car—this beat-up Honda Civic I had in high school—had a really easy plate, it started with ABC, literally. But this one I have now, well, it's a 2012, but the plate makes no sense. 

Plus, the screen on the parking meter was so scratched up, like someone took a key to it, so I couldn't even see if I typed the numbers right. I tried downloading the app they advertise on the side of the machine, but my phone had no service right there. I ended up just guessing, and I still got a ticket! It's like forty-five dollars for a parking ticket now. Which is ridiculous, especially since Brenda at the clinic is always sending us home early if the afternoon schedule is light, so my paychecks have been short. It's like, how am I supposed to pay a forty-five dollar ticket when I'm missing three hours of pay on a Tuesday? 

But, um... wait. Sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, if I enjoy anything. Yeah, no. I ended up just driving home without even going into the comic shop. Nothing really sounds fun anyway.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or ending your life?

No... no, I don't really think about doing that. I mean, I just feel heavy and tired all the time, but I wouldn't actually hurt myself on purpose. 

I did almost get hurt by accident at the clinic on Thursday, though. They installed these new sharps containers in all the exam rooms, and the maintenance guy who put them up definitely used the wrong drywall anchors. So in room three, the whole plastic box is just sort of sagging off the wall. I was trying to drop a needle in there after a blood draw, and the whole thing shifted. I swear I thought it was going to crash right onto my foot. Which would have been really bad because I was wearing these cheap mesh sneakers. 

I bought them on clearance at this outlet mall a few towns over. Have you ever been to one of those? It's one of those outdoor malls, which is just a terrible design because when it rains, you're getting completely soaked just walking from store to store. And the food court was completely outside too, just a bunch of metal tables with umbrellas that don't even block the wind. I bought a soft pretzel there and it was cold before I even took a bite. Just rock hard and covered in way too much salt. I had to throw half of it in the trash, which felt like a waste of six bucks. The seagulls were swarming the garbage cans, too, just making this awful screeching noise... 

But, um, yeah. No, I don't want to end my life or anything. I just... I just feel really tired.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Um, nervous? Not really. I don't feel on edge or anything like that. It's more just... flat, you know? Like everything is just gray. 

Though, my mom is always telling me I should drink less coffee because she thinks it makes me nervous. She's really into all these herbal teas right now. She keeps bringing over these little boxes of chamomile and peppermint from this weird health food store she found. It's in this strip mall right next to a dry cleaner, and honestly, the whole store smells like those chemicals they use to press shirts. It's so overpowering. I went in there with her once to buy some sort of organic honey, and the guy working the register was just staring at his phone the entire time. Didn't even look up when he handed us the receipt. And the honey wasn't even in a normal squeeze bottle, it was in this heavy glass jar with a cork in it. Like, who puts a cork in a honey jar? Every time I try to get it open, my hands get all sticky, and then I have to wash them, but the soap dispenser in my bathroom is broken. The little pump part just snapped right off last week when I was washing my hands after taking out the trash. 

The trash bags I bought are terrible, by the way. They're supposed to be tear-resistant, but the second you put a pizza box in there, the whole side rips open. I had to double-bag the last one, and it still leaked coffee grounds all over the hallway carpet. 

But, uh, no. I don't really feel nervous. Just tired.
Are there any small things that happen during the day that you look forward to?

Um, look forward to? No, not really. I don't really have anything like that. I wake up and just kind of... wait for the day to be over. 

I guess I used to look forward to lunch at the clinic, but Brenda changed the lunch schedule last month. She moved me from the noon slot to 1:30, which is just way too late. By the time I get to the break room, all the good chairs are taken. There's this one leather chair in the corner that's actually comfortable, but the billing coordinator, Dave, always claims it. He sits there for his entire hour, just scrolling through his phone with the volume on high. He watches these weird restoration videos, like where guys take rusty old axes and polish them until they look brand new. And he doesn't use headphones! I asked him once if he could turn it down, and he just glared at me. 

Plus, the microwave in there is disgusting. Someone exploded a bowl of chili in it like two weeks ago and nobody wiped it down. It's just baked onto the ceiling of the microwave now. Every time you heat something up, the whole room smells like burnt beans. I tried bringing cold sandwiches instead, but the deli down the street from my apartment raised their prices. It used to be five dollars for a turkey club, and now it's almost nine. Nine dollars for a sandwich! And they don't even use real mayonnaise anymore, it's this weird vegan spread that tastes like cardboard. 

So yeah, no... I don't really look forward to anything. It's all just kind of exhausting.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Weight? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my clothes still fit the same, so I haven't really lost any weight. I haven't really been paying attention to it, honestly. 

I did have to buy new scrub pants for work, though. The ones the clinic gave us when I started were this awful stiff material. They felt like wearing cardboard, and the drawstring was way too short. Every time I washed them, the string would get lost inside the waistband, and I'd have to spend like twenty minutes fishing it out with a safety pin. I finally gave up and went to this uniform supply store on the other side of town. The parking lot there is a nightmare. The spaces are painted so close together, I could barely open my car door. The guy parked next to me had this massive truck with a lift kit, and his tires were practically over the line. I had to squeeze out of my car like a contortionist, and I ended up getting this weird grease smudge on my jacket from his door handle. 

And the store itself was freezing. They had the AC blasting like it was the middle of summer, even though it was only like fifty degrees outside. I was shivering the whole time I was trying on pants. I ended up buying three pairs of these dark blue ones, but when I got home, I realized the pockets are completely fake. Like, they have a seam where a pocket should be, but it's just sewn shut. Who makes scrub pants without pockets? Where am I supposed to put my pens? I had to buy this little plastic pocket protector thing to clip onto my shirt, but it keeps falling off whenever I bend over to take someone's blood pressure...

But, um, no. My weight is pretty much the same. Just... normal, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Sleeping? Um, no, not really. I sleep fine, I guess. 

I mean, my mattress is terrible, but I still sleep. I got it from this guy on Craigslist when I first got my apartment, and he promised it was basically brand new, but there's this huge dip right in the middle. I tried putting a piece of plywood under it to make it firmer, but the plywood I bought at the hardware store was slightly too long. I had to strap it to the roof of my car to get it home, and the twine they gave me was so cheap it started fraying before I even left the parking lot. I was so paranoid it was going to fly off and hit the car behind me. It was this really nice, shiny black BMW, too. I don't know why someone with a car like that was driving so close to me anyway. People in this town tailgate like crazy. 

Especially on that stretch of road right near the clinic where the speed limit drops from 45 to 25 for absolutely no reason. The cops just sit behind the billboard there waiting to pull people over. They got one of the nurses I work with last week, and she was so mad she complained about it for our entire shift. She wouldn't stop talking about how the radar gun must have been broken and how she was going to fight the ticket in court. She even printed out all these satellite maps of the road to prove the speed limit sign was obscured by a tree branch. She left the papers sitting on the break room table for days, right next to that disgusting microwave. 

But, um... yeah. Sleep is fine. I don't have trouble falling asleep or anything.
Do you feel like you have enough energy to do the things you need to do?

Energy? Um... no, not really. Even if I have a day off or sleep in late, my body just feels completely worn out. By the time I finish rooming patients and catching up on all the charts at work, I have absolutely nothing left in the tank. I can't even bring myself to do laundry, or go shoot hoops, or mess around with any of my electronics stuff like I used to. 

I actually tried to fix this old radio last weekend. It's one of those vintage ones with the wooden casing that my grandpa gave me before he passed away. I bought a new soldering iron for it because my old one got ruined. I had let my buddy borrow it a few months ago to fix some wiring in his car, and he brought it back with the tip completely melted and covered in this black gunk. He said he accidentally dropped it on a piece of plastic trim, but honestly, I don't know how you mess up a soldering iron that badly. He's always breaking things, though. Last year, he borrowed my power drill and somehow managed to strip the gears inside. He tried to tell me it was defective, but it was a brand new DeWalt! They don't just break like that. 

Anyway, I bought this new iron online, but the shipping took forever. The tracking said it was sitting at a facility just two towns over for like four days. I don't understand how a package can just sit there. Do they just throw it in a corner and forget about it? And when it finally arrived, the box looked like it had been run over by a forklift. Luckily the iron inside was fine, but still. You'd think for what they charge for shipping these days, they'd take better care of the packages. 

So yeah, I sat down to work on the radio, but after like ten minutes, I just... I couldn't focus. My arms felt heavy, and I just ended up staring at the circuit board until I put it all away. It's just too exhausting.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt better and were interested in things again?

Better? Like... interested in things? Um, no, I don't think so. It's just been like this for... I don't even know how long. 

I mean, I thought I was getting interested in something when I bought that new soldering iron, but that was just a waste of money. I should have known better, honestly. I always buy stuff thinking it'll fix things. Like last month, I bought this fancy new coffee maker. It was one of those ones that grinds the beans right before it brews. I thought maybe if I had better coffee, I'd feel a little more awake in the mornings. But the grinder on it is so incredibly loud. The first time I used it, it sounded like a wood chipper going off in my kitchen. It literally startled my neighbor's dog through the wall, and the dog started barking, which woke up the guy who lives upstairs. He's this older guy who works night shifts at the bottling plant, and he gets really aggressive if his sleep is disturbed. He came down and pounded on my door at like 6:00 AM, yelling about the noise. He was wearing these really ratty plaid pajama pants and a faded t-shirt from some rock concert in the 80s. I tried to apologize, but he just kept going off about how thin the walls are and how the landlord refuses to put in proper insulation. 

He's right about the insulation, though. In the winter, my apartment is freezing. I have to wrap my windows in that plastic shrink wrap stuff just to keep the drafts out. You have to use a hair dryer to shrink it tight, and my hair dryer is so old it barely gets hot anymore. It just blows this lukewarm air, so it takes me like an hour to do one window. And if you leave the hair dryer on too long, it starts smelling like burning dust...

But, um, no. I haven't really had any times where I felt better. It's just... this.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite lately?

Appetite? Um, no, not really. I mean, I eat about the same, I guess. Nothing's really changed there.

I did try to make spaghetti the other night, though. I bought this jar of sauce that was supposed to be, like, authentic Italian or whatever. It was on sale at the grocery store. But when I went to open it, the lid was stuck on so tight I couldn't get it off. I tried running it under hot water, tapping it with a butter knife, everything. I even used one of those rubber grip pad things that my mom gave me when I moved out. She gave me a whole box of random kitchen stuff—like three different kinds of spatulas and a garlic press that I've literally never used. Who even presses garlic? You can just buy it minced in a jar. 

Anyway, I finally got the sauce open, but my hand slipped and I spilled half of it all over the counter. It stained the grout between the tiles, and I spent like twenty minutes scrubbing it with a toothbrush. It's one of those electric toothbrushes, too, but the battery is basically dead so it just vibrates really weakly. I need to buy replacement heads for it, but they're so expensive at the pharmacy near my place. Everything there is marked up. I went in there last week just to buy some ibuprofen and it was like eight dollars for a tiny bottle. The cashier was this kid who looked like he was still in high school, and he was completely ignoring me because he was texting on his phone. He had one of those cases with the pop-socket things on the back, and it was shaped like a piece of pizza. It was just really unprofessional.

But, yeah, my appetite is fine. I ended up just eating the plain noodles with butter. It was whatever.
Do you find yourself moving or reacting more slowly than you used to?

Moving slower? Um... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I walk at my normal pace at work, I guess. 

I did buy these new shoes for the clinic recently, though, because my old ones were totally worn out on the heels. They're supposed to be those special slip-resistant ones that nurses wear, but they squeak so loud on the linoleum floors. Every time I walk down the hall to grab a patient, it's just this constant squeaking. It drives the front desk receptionist, Brenda, absolutely crazy. But she complains about literally everything anyway. Just on Tuesday, she spent like twenty minutes complaining loudly because the vending machine in the breakroom ate her dollar. It's one of those older machines where the metal coils don't spin all the way, so her bag of pretzels just got stuck dangling right on the edge. 

I tried to help her by shaking the machine to knock it loose, but the maintenance guy apparently bolted it to the wall last month. I don't know why you'd bolt a vending machine to the wall. It's not like anyone is going to steal it. The thing weighs like a thousand pounds. Plus, the snacks inside are always stale anyway. I bought a pack of peanut butter crackers from it once and they tasted exactly like cardboard. They expired back in February, which is ridiculous because the vendor is supposed to come restock it every other week. 

But, um, no, I don't think I'm moving or reacting any slower than I usually do.
Do you feel like your thoughts are slower than they used to be?

Slower thoughts? Um... yeah, I guess so. Like, at work I’ll be staring at a patient’s intake screen and I just have to reread the same line over and over again. 

Though, to be fair, our monitors are terrible. They updated the clinic's software last month, and now the font is incredibly tiny. The IT guy, Kevin, came in to supposedly fix it, but he just ended up talking about his hydroponic garden for like forty-five minutes. He grows all these weird heirloom tomatoes in his basement, and he brought a whole grocery bag full of them into the breakroom. They were all lumpy and had these weird green stripes on them. Brenda threw them in the trash as soon as he left because she said basement tomatoes are a health hazard. Which is funny coming from her, because she leaves her dirty coffee mugs in the sink for days. There's this one mug she has with a picture of a cartoon cat hanging from a branch that says "Hang in there!" and the inside of it is completely stained dark brown. I tried to wash it once because I needed to use the sink, but the sponge in the breakroom smelled like pure mildew. It’s one of those yellow sponges with the green scrubby side, but the scrubby part is completely peeling off. I don't know why the office manager doesn't just buy a new pack of sponges. They're like two dollars. 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I've been catching myself missing little details on the charts, like medication doses, or I'll just completely mix up what I was about to ask the patient next. It just takes my brain a lot longer to process things now.
Do you feel like you're having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Concentrating? Um... well, yeah, I kind of just mentioned that, actually. Like with the intake screens. I'll just sit there staring at it and have to read the exact same sentence over and over again because it just doesn't stick in my head. 

And, like, I've been messing up little things on the charts, too. Like missing the medication doses, or I'll go into the exam room and completely forget what I was supposed to ask the patient next. I just stand there holding the blood pressure cuff looking like an idiot. 

Which reminds me, we actually need new cuffs at the clinic. The velcro on the adult-sized ones is completely worn out, so when you pump it up, it just pops right off the patient's arm. It happened to me yesterday with this guy who came in for a physical. He was wearing this really weird cologne that smelled exactly like pine needles and gasoline. It was so strong it gave me a headache for the rest of my shift. I tried to take some ibuprofen, but like I said, I didn't want to buy any at that pharmacy because of the kid with the pizza phone case, so I had to ask Brenda if she had any. She did, but she keeps them loose at the bottom of her purse. Just, like, rolling around with old receipts and pennies. I had to wipe lint off the pill before I swallowed it. It was disgusting. 

But yeah, my concentration is definitely shot. I just keep missing details and forgetting what I'm doing.
Do you feel like you're physically slowing down in your daily activities?

Physically slowing down? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, you kind of just asked me about moving slower, right? Like I said, I walk at my normal pace. 

But honestly, the floors at the clinic make it hard to walk fast anyway. They just put down this new wax over the weekend, and it is incredibly slippery. Like, dangerously slippery. One of the other medical assistants, Sarah, almost totally wiped out near the breakroom yesterday. She was carrying this massive stack of sample medication boxes—the ones the drug reps always leave behind. We have this one rep, this guy named Todd, who always brings these really elaborate catered lunches just to talk about some new asthma inhaler. Last time he brought this huge tray of sandwiches from that deli down on 4th Street, but he didn't label any of them, so nobody knew which ones had mayo. Brenda is severely allergic to eggs, so she just stood there glaring at the sandwiches for like ten minutes before she finally just ate a bag of chips from the vending machine. The same vending machine that ate her dollar, actually. 

But yeah, Sarah almost dropped like fifty boxes of inhaler samples right in the middle of the hallway because of the floor wax. So you kind of have to shuffle around carefully so you don't break your neck. 

But no, I don't feel like I'm personally slowing down physically or anything. Just trying not to fall, I guess.
Do you find it harder to initiate activities or tasks than you used to?

Harder to start things? Yeah, I mean... it’s just that I’m so tired. Like, even after a day off or sleeping late, my body still just feels completely worn out. By the time I finish rooming patients and catching up on all those charts I was talking about, it feels like I have absolutely nothing left in the tank to do my laundry, or go shoot hoops, or even mess with my electronics stuff. 

Which is annoying because I have this old retro console I was trying to fix up. I needed a specific soldering iron for it, so I ordered one online, but the delivery guy just left it out in the rain instead of putting it under the awning on the porch. The box was completely soaked. It smelled exactly like wet dog and cardboard. I tried to complain to the shipping company, but their customer service line is just an endless robot menu. You press 'four' for damaged packages, and it literally just loops you right back to the main menu. I was on hold for like an hour listening to this terrible elevator music. It was that one song, 'The Girl from Ipanema', but played on a really cheap-sounding synth keyboard. I ended up just hanging up because my phone battery was at like two percent. 

Which, actually, my phone charger is another thing that's broken. The wire is completely frayed at the base, so you have to bend it at this very specific, weird angle just to get it to charge. 

But, um... what did you ask me? Oh, starting tasks. Yeah. I just don't have the energy to even start fixing the console or dealing with any of that anyway. Or doing my laundry, honestly. I just feel way too worn out.
Do you find yourself wanting to be around other people less often than you used to?

Wanting to be around people less? Um... I don't know, maybe? I haven't really thought about it. I guess I just haven't been doing much of anything lately, with anyone. 

Like I was saying about the basketball thing, I used to go down to the courts at the park a couple times a week. There's this group of guys who are always there on Tuesdays and Thursdays. But the city just changed the lights they use at the park. They took down the old yellow ones and put up these incredibly bright, harsh LED ones. It literally looks like a stadium now, but the light is so white it kind of messes with your depth perception when you're trying to shoot. Plus, they attract so many bugs. Like, massive swarms of moths just circling the bulbs all night. 

One of the guys, Marcus, he actually swallowed a bug by accident last time I was there. He was going up for a layup and just started choking and coughing. He had to go over to the water fountain, but the water fountain at that park is always broken. It either has zero pressure, so you have to put your mouth right on the metal part—which is gross—or it shoots up like a geyser and gets your whole shirt wet. Marcus got the geyser. He was soaked. And it was pretty chilly that night, too. 

Anyway, I haven't been back to the courts in a while. Not really because of the guys or anything. I just... I don't know, I just haven't felt like going out.
Do you feel like you no longer enjoy things you used to, or that you're unable to experience pleasure?

Enjoying things? Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, I don't really know. Like I said, I just haven't been doing much of anything. I haven't been playing basketball or messing with my electronics. 

Oh, actually, speaking of electronics, my buddy Dave texted me the other day about this vintage arcade cabinet he found at a garage sale. It was an original Pac-Man machine, like, the full-size stand-up one. But the guy selling it had kept it in his barn for like twenty years, so it was completely covered in dust and spiderwebs. Dave said he opened the back panel and found a literal bird's nest inside next to the motherboard. Not even an old one, either—there were still little bits of blue eggshells in it. And the joystick was completely seized up. He tried to clean it with some WD-40, but he accidentally sprayed it all over the front glass instead. So now the glass is all greasy and smells like a mechanic's shop. 

He wanted me to come over and help him figure out the wiring for the coin slot, because he wants to set it up so you actually have to put quarters in it to play. Which I think is kind of dumb, honestly, because who even carries quarters anymore? Unless you go to the laundromat, I guess. The laundromat near my apartment has this one machine that always eats your quarters. It's machine number four. Everyone in the building knows about it, but the landlord refuses to put an 'out of order' sign on it. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, enjoying things. Yeah, I don't know. I just haven't really felt like doing any of that stuff lately anyway. Just haven't had the energy for it.

The laundromat near my apartment has this one machine that always eats your quarters. It's machine number four. Everyone in the building knows about it, but the landlord refuses to put an 'out of order' sign on it. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, enjoying things. Yeah, I don't know. I just haven't really felt like doing any of that stuff lately anyway. Just haven't had the energy for it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, and significant changes in motivation and energy levels, which have been present for over two years. These symptoms align with the criteria for a Major Depressive Disorder, specifically the single episode type, given the duration and impact on daily functioning.
